{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"On a rainy Tuesday, Eli discovered a tiny door behind the bookcase in the town library. He had been searching for a book about moths when one heavy volume slipped from the shelf. Behind it, a green-painted door no taller than his knee stood slightly ajar.

Eli called to Ms. Rowan, the librarian. She crouched beside him and brushed dust from a brass handle. “I’ve worked here thirty years,” she whispered. “I’ve never seen this before.”

The door opened onto a narrow staircase. Together, they climbed to a small room tucked beneath the library roof. Sunlight slipped through a round window, illuminating shelves filled with handwritten notebooks.

Ms. Rowan opened one. Inside were drawings of birds, maps of the town, and notes from children who had visited the library decades ago. One page described a pond that had vanished when a road was built. Another listed the names of every tree in the park.

At the bottom of the last notebook, someone had written: “Leave a little knowledge for whoever comes next.”

Eli looked around. “Can we add something?”

Ms. Rowan found a blank notebook in a drawer. Eli wrote about the moths he had been studying, including where they rested during the day and which flowers attracted them. Ms. Rowan added a note about the library’s oldest books.

They placed the new notebook beside the others. Then Eli chose a book about moths and tucked it under his arm.

The next week, he returned with a drawing of a silver-striped moth. In the hidden room, a fresh page waited for it."}
